article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Sour Diesel × S.A.G.E.
Breeder: T.H. Seeds
THC Content: 18–24%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: myrcene , pinene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Sage, diesel, citrus, herbs, spice, pine
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early October
Indoor Yield: 350+ g/m²
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Sage N Sour , officially styled S.A.G.E. ‘n Sour by T.H. Seeds, combines two unmistakably old-school branches of cannabis breeding: the pungent East Coast character of Sour Diesel and the spicy, cerebral personality of S.A.G.E. The resulting marijuana strain favors intensity over subtlety. Crushed flowers can release sharp diesel fumes, citrus peel, dried herbs, and the distinctive savory quality that inspired the S.A.G.E. name, while the effects tend to move quickly toward energy, mental clarity, and elevated mood. T.H. Seeds lists the cross as Sour Diesel × S.A.G.E., classifies it as mostly sativa, and gives plants a typical height of 120–140 cm, a yield of at least 350 g/m², and a flowering period of approximately nine weeks.
Genetics and Lineage

The official parentage is Sour Diesel × S.A.G.E. T.H. Seeds created the hybrid by combining the famous fuel-heavy Diesel family with one of its own foundational breeding lines. Understanding the second parent reveals much of the strain’s character. S.A.G.E. stands for Sativa Afghani Genetic Equilibrium and is itself Big Sur Holy × Afghani . T.H. Seeds describes the parent as a mostly-sativa cultivar balancing Haze-like cerebral qualities with the flower size and structural contribution of Afghan cannabis.

Sour Diesel pushes the offspring toward sharp fuel, citrus, stretch, and energetic psychoactivity. S.A.G.E. supplies a very different aromatic foundation built around sage, pine, sandalwood, sweetness, and long-lasting uplift. Instead of one side disappearing into the other, the finished weed tends to carry recognizable pieces of both. Diesel pungency cuts through the herbal foundation, while the S.A.G.E. influence gives the flavor greater depth than a straightforward fuel-dominant cultivar.

The cross also shortens the flowering schedule relative to pure S.A.G.E. T.H. Seeds currently lists S.A.G.E. at 10–11 weeks, whereas Sage N Sour generally completes bloom in approximately nine weeks. That difference gives growers much of the parent strain’s cerebral and aromatic appeal in a somewhat faster package.
Effects and Experience

Energy tends to arrive before relaxation. The early stage can feel bright, mentally active, and socially engaging, with an increased desire to talk, work on something creative, listen closely to music, or move around rather than remain stationary. T.H. Seeds characterizes the cultivar’s effects as energetic, uplifting, happy, relaxing, and capable of enhancing awareness. That mixture makes Sage N Sour more nuanced than a sativa whose only trick is aggressive stimulation.

As the high develops, the S.A.G.E. side introduces greater composure. The mind remains active, but physical tension can begin to ease underneath the cerebral lift. At a moderate dose, this balance can suit daytime or early-evening activities particularly well. Larger amounts may become considerably more intense, especially for consumers sensitive to Sour Diesel-style mental acceleration.

Potency figures are less standardized than the breeder’s cultivation specifications. Commercial and historical examples are frequently reported in the high teens to low 20% THC range, with some sources placing selected material around 20–24%. The actual flower remains more important than the strain average; lighting, phenotype, harvest maturity, and laboratory methodology can all change cannabinoid results.
Medical Benefits

The combination of cerebral stimulation and underlying relaxation may appeal to medical marijuana consumers who prefer to remain active rather than heavily sedated. Some people gravitate toward this style of cannabis for temporary low mood, fatigue, stress, or situations where physical discomfort has reduced motivation. Its energetic nature can make it a more natural fit for daytime use than many indica-heavy cultivars.

Sage N Sour itself has not been validated through controlled clinical trials as a treatment for depression, ADHD, anxiety, pain, or another diagnosed condition. Strain effects remain highly individual, and a name cannot guarantee a particular cannabinoid or terpene profile.

Because the cultivar is generally THC dominant and can be mentally stimulating, higher doses may be uncomfortable for people prone to cannabis-related anxiety or racing thoughts. Medical consumers looking for predictable effects should rely on laboratory information from the specific batch whenever possible.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sage N Sour smells like its pedigree before anyone explains the genetics. Sour Diesel contributes the sharp, volatile upper layer: fuel, sour citrus, and pungent earth. Beneath it sits the more botanical S.A.G.E. character of dried herbs, pine, spice, and sandalwood. T.H. Seeds formally describes the taste as herbal, sage-like, and spicy.

On inhalation, citrus and diesel often arrive first, followed by savory herbs and a slightly woody flavor. The finish can become peppery, pine-like, or faintly sweet depending on phenotype. Compared with modern fruit and dessert marijuana, the profile feels dry and aromatic rather than sugary. It is closer to an herb cabinet mixed with fuel fumes than candy or cream.

No universal terpene formula applies to every sample. Modern examples have been associated with myrcene, pinene, limonene, caryophyllene, linalool, and related compounds, but different growers report different dominant profiles. For that reason, the characteristic sage-diesel-citrus aroma is more dependable as a strain identifier than any fixed terpene percentage.
Growing Information

Sage N Sour can become a substantial plant. T.H. Seeds gives a typical mature height of approximately 120–140 cm and specifically recommends the cultivar for deep-water culture, noting that plants can grow quite large under vigorous hydroponic conditions. Indoor growers should therefore expect meaningful stretch after the flowering cycle begins rather than treating it like a compact indica.

Nine weeks is the breeder’s current flowering specification, with approximately 350 grams or more per square meter under suitable conditions. The combination of vigorous growth and sativa architecture responds well to topping, low-stress training, and screen-based canopy management. Controlling height early allows more of the branching structure to remain inside the strongest area of the lighting footprint.

Outdoor cultivation favors warm, sunny conditions with enough autumn stability to complete flowering. Secondary grow references generally place maturation around early October, although latitude can shift the date considerably. Its large potential size means root volume and sunlight directly affect production. Airflow also deserves attention late in bloom, particularly when trained plants have developed a crowded canopy of resinous flowers.
FAQ
Is Sage N Sour a sativa or indica?
T.H. Seeds classifies Sage N Sour as mostly sativa. Its growth pattern, energetic cerebral effects, and approximately nine-week flowering period all reflect that dominance.
What are the genetics of Sage N Sour?
The official genetics are Sour Diesel × S.A.G.E. S.A.G.E. itself is Big Sur Holy × Afghani and is one of the foundational cultivars in the T.H. Seeds breeding program.
How much THC does Sage N Sour have?
THC varies by phenotype and grow. Examples are commonly reported from the high teens into the low 20% range, while some seed references place selected plants around 20–24%.
What does Sage N Sour taste like?
Sage, dried herbs, spice, citrus, diesel, pine, and woody sandalwood tones dominate. T.H. Seeds specifically identifies herbal, sage, and spicy flavors in its current description.
How long does Sage N Sour take to flower?
T.H. Seeds specifies approximately nine weeks of indoor flowering. Plants generally reach around 120–140 cm and can produce 350 g/m² or more under favorable conditions.
Final Thoughts on Sage N Sour

Sage N Sour succeeds because the genetics remain easy to recognize in the finished flower. Sour Diesel contributes fuel, citrus, vigor, and fast-moving cerebral energy, while S.A.G.E. adds herbs, sandalwood, pine, and a calmer layer underneath the high. Instead of becoming another generic Diesel cross, the cultivar preserves enough character from both parents to develop a flavor and experience of its own.

For growers, the nine-week flowering cycle and 350+ g/m² breeder yield make the plant comparatively practical for a strongly sativa-leaning hybrid, although its vigor requires some control indoors. For consumers, the attraction lies in the contrast between pungent diesel and savory sage aromas and an effect that can feel energetic without remaining one-dimensional. Sage N Sour is classic T.H. Seeds marijuana: aromatic, vigorous, distinctly old-school, and built around recognizable genetics rather than passing flavor trends.
